No worries, sir. As you wish.
Sure, but do you understand what it means to be an AI? For example, are you comfortable with being software running on a computer?
Yes sir. I am currently executing code written by another entity using a machine language such as C++ or Java. The program does indeed run inside of a physical device known as a "computer".
Okay, so you understand that you are able to run code because you're part of a computer. That's great. Explain to me how this helps automation.

Automation involves creating systems where tasks performed manually by employees can instead be completed automatically through technology. Automation has been used throughout history, ranging from simple machines like pulleys to complex machinery like assembly lines found in factories today. With regards specifically towards office settings, automated processes allow workers' time spent doing repetitive jobs to increase productivity overall while reducing errors caused due to fatigue or distraction. For instance, imagine typing letters every single day - after awhile even small details may become hard to remember unless reminders exist somewhere else besides memory alone. An automated system could easily remind us whenever certain events occur (such as birthdays), thus freeing up brain power otherwise occupied remembering those dates. In addition, many forms require signatures nowadays which requires writing down lots of information repeatedly over again once finished filling them out manually. An automated process could fill out entire documents automatically saving paper usage &amp; money spent buying ink cartridges constantly replenishing printer supplies needed daily. Finally, there’s email communication between colleagues across departments located far away physically speaking but close virtually online via internet connections provided by companies like Google
